The method addresses the slow rendering speed of original NeRFs by factorizing appearance into view-independent coefficients (stored in a PlenOctree) and view-dependent basis functions (SHs) [S2].

The claim states that the method addresses slow rendering speed by factorizing appearance into view-independent coefficients (stored in a PlenOctree) and view-dependent basis functions (SHs). The evidence explicitly confirms this: it mentions that NeRF-SH factorizes appearance via spherical harmonic basis functions, where weights (view-independent) are a function of point p and basis functions are a function of viewing direction. It states the MLP regresses view-independent information (density and SH coefficients) stored in a PlenOctree. It also confirms this accelerates rendering by more than 3000 times, addressing the speed issue.

NeRF-SH is a variant of Neural Radiance Fields that replaces the direct RGB output with spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients, allowing the neural network to predict only view-independent density and appearance weights while deferring view-dependent color calculation to a closed-form basis evaluation [S1, unofficial][S2].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in both sources. Source [S1] explicitly states that NeRF-SH modifies the NeRF network to predict spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients and density instead of raw RGB values, which eliminates the need for view-direction input (view-independent prediction) and calculates color via SH basis evaluation (closed-form basis evaluation). Source [S2] corroborates this by describing the factorization of appearance where the MLP regresses view-independent information (density and SH coefficients) and view-dependent color is determined by querying spherical harmonic functions at inference.
